extracted.intended_audience: eRA Commons users and administrators (signing officials, account administrators, administrative officials, principal investigators, and other organizational administrative staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and policy requirements for creating, editing, affiliating, and managing eRA Commons user accounts, passwords, roles, and delegations within an organization. Covers who may perform actions, required fields, role constraints, search-before-create workflow, and delegation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary password validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Temporary passwords, sent to the user via email, are only valid for 48 hours and must be changed to a permanent password of the user’s choosing within that time period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The temporary password is emailed to the address in the user profile; user must log in with it and immediately create a new password. If not used within 48 hours, it expires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Password Policy validation
rubrics_metrics.description: All passwords are validated against the Password Policy requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the referenced NIH eRA Password Policy document (http://www.era.nih.gov/files/NIH_eRA_Password_Policy.pdf) for exact complexity/format rules; the Change Password screen lists password creation standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use browser 'save password' option
rubrics_metrics.description: For security purposes and to maintain the integrity of your account, you should never use the save password option and should always re-enter your password whenever you log in to Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated warning: recommended not to use browser's save password; old passwords may re-appear if browser cache/history not cleared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Browser cache/history caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Your old password might re-appear in the Password field if you have not cleared your browser's cache/history, especially if you had previously opted to save the password in the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsure whether the password field contains the new password, clear cache/history and log in again with the new password.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change password workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: You can change your password anytime you are logged in as long as you know your current password using the Change Password screen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access Change Password via Admin module or Person icon; enter current password and the new password (and confirmation); passwords display as dots; submit to effect change immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual password change requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You are still required to change your eRA Commons password annually even if you use Login.gov to log into Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even after using two-factor authentication providers that meet NIH standards, Commons will prompt for an annual password change; see relevant FAQs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expired password reset process
rubrics_metrics.description: When your password has expired or has been reset, you will be directed to select a new password when you try to log in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter current password, enter new password, confirm new password, and submit; the new password must conform to screen-listed standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account lockout policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If you attempt to log into eRA Commons five consecutive times within a 60-minute period using an invalid eRA Commons password, your account will lock.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lockout lasts 15 minutes. After 15 minutes, an SO or account administrator can reset the password; the user can also use the 'Forgot Password/Locked Account?' link if they remember and can access the associated email.

rubrics_metrics.name: Email association requirement for password resets
rubrics_metrics.description: Because your temporary password will be sent to the email address stored in eRA Commons, you must remember which email is associated with your eRA Commons account and have access to log into it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you don't have access to that email, contact an SO or AA to reset password and change the email where reset emails are sent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admin module access and role-determined privileges
rubrics_metrics.description: All Commons users have access to the Admin module, however, your role determines what you can and cannot do within the module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admin includes Account Management, Delegations, ESI Eligibility searches (SO/AO only). Certain functions (e.g., creating SO accounts) are limited to specific roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search-before-create requirement to avoid duplicate accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: You cannot create a new account until you perform a search for the account first; this measure helps avoid the creation of duplicate accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Create New Account button becomes enabled only after performing the search. Use the percent (%) wildcard for partial matches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may create accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Only an organization's eRA Commons administrators can create an account. Individual PIs or other eRA users cannot create their own account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need a new account or account assistance, contact an SO from your organization; procedures for invitation, appointment, or institutional registration also exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role-based account creation permissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific administrative roles can create certain account types: SO can create accounts of any role type except IAR and can create additional SO accounts; AO, AA, BO can create many account types but have restrictions (cannot create SO, BO, FCOI, or IAR depending on role).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See role definitions: SO (signing official), AO (administrative official), AA (account administrator), BO (business official) for exact creation permissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required fields when creating an account
rubrics_metrics.description: On the Create Account screen, all fields except Middle Name are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required fields include User Type, User ID (unique and unchangeable), Primary Organization (defaults to creator’s org and cannot be changed), Last Name, First Name, Email, Confirm Email, plus roles selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: User ID immutability
rubrics_metrics.description: The User ID is not changeable after account creation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take care when entering the system user ID during account creation because it cannot be modified later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary organization defaults and immutability
rubrics_metrics.description: The Primary Organization field defaults to your organization and cannot be changed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an individual needs to be affiliated with your organization but already has a non-administrative account with another organization (e.g., PI), affiliate their existing account instead of creating a new one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Email for password resets must be accessible
rubrics_metrics.description: The Email entered during account creation will be used for password resets; it is very important to enter an email that the user will ALWAYS have access to, which might be their personal email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two emails are sent when account is created: one with temporary password and one with the user ID. Changing this email affects where 'Forgot Password' messages go.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role assignment required at creation
rubrics_metrics.description: After entering contact information, you must assign a role to the account; if you do not add a role, you get an error when you try to save the new user.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use + Add Roles button; organization defaults to your organization. Only roles appropriate to your administrative privilege (e.g., only an SO can assign SO role) appear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting multiple roles and UI tips
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Ctrl+click to select multiple roles (Shift+click for contiguous selections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you made a mistake adding roles, you can remove them via the Remove button in the Actions column before saving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicting roles prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Be sure to add ONLY scientific (PI, POSTDOC, etc.) OR administrative (SO, AA, etc.) roles to an account, but not both, as they are incompatible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some roles conflict (e.g., PD/PI cannot co-exist with an SO); an error message occurs when saving if conflicting roles are assigned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliate existing PI accounts rather than create new
rubrics_metrics.description: If the person already has a PI or other scientific role account, you should affiliate the person to your organization instead of creating a new account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIs and other scientific roles are intended to be used throughout an investigator's career regardless of institutional affiliation; affiliate via Admin/Account Management when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing restrictions on existing accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: When editing an account, you can no longer change the User ID or name. You can, however, edit the email, roles, affiliation, or reset the password.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Manage on the account record to perform these edits. To unaffiliate a user from your organization, use the Unaffiliate button; you cannot unaffiliate someone from their prior organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search tips and wildcard usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the percent character (%) as a wildcard. By default the Search only within my organization checkbox is not marked (searches all organizations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When searching outside your organization you must include Last Name or Commons ID. If accounts appear, you can click Name to view Funding Support/employment history to help disambiguate duplicate names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliate only scientific accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: You can affiliate only those with scientific (research-related) accounts (such as PI), not those with administrative accounts (such as SO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To affiliate, find person via search, click Manage, then Affiliate; the Affiliate button only appears if the user is not currently affiliated with your organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot unaffiliate a user from their prior organization
rubrics_metrics.description: You can affiliate the person with your organization, but you cannot unaffiliate a person with their prior organization. Only an administrator from the prior organization can unaffiliate a user from that organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan transitions accordingly; affiliation changes require cooperation from the prior institution for full removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous Submission Eligibility advanced search rules
rubrics_metrics.description: When performing an advanced search for PIs with continuous submission eligibility, you can search within your organization or include those outside of your organization; the percent sign (%) can be used as a wildcard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Search within your organization checkbox is marked by default. When searching outside your organization you must include Last Name or Commons ID; search results show CS Eligibility, User ID, Email, Account Status, Role, Institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting a new Signing Official (SO) account prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: To initiate an SO account creation request with the eRA Service Desk, the organization's SAM.gov registration status must be active, the Electronic Business Point of Contact (eBiz POC) associated with SAM.gov must still be active at the organization, and the eBiz POC must still have access to the email address associated to the active SAM.gov registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The eBiz POC must contact the eRA Service Desk using their registered email address to request a new SO account; the Service Desk evaluates and vets the request against SAM.gov records.

rubrics_metrics.name: SO account creation by Service Desk and follow-up actions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the eRA Service Desk grants a new SO account request, they will gather necessary information, create the account, and the new SO will receive two emails (Commons ID and temporary password) and should immediately log into eRA Commons and change their password.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because organizations should maintain at least two SOs, the new SO should create another SO account for a second member.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegations overview and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Delegation is the method of assigning (and revoking) authority to other Commons users from the same organization to enter/process grant information, update Personal Profile information, submit RPPR information, and work with specific modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegations can be for an individual's own account or an administrative user can delegate on behalf of another user; delegations are not permanent and can be revoked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency-specific restriction on delegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Delegations cannot be used for Department of Commerce (DOC) and SAMHSA awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attempting to use Delegations for DOC or SAMHSA awards is not supported; follow agency-specific instructions when working with those awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation authorities table (who can delegate what to whom)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different authority types (e.g., Progress Report, Sponsor, Status, PPF, Submit, xTrain) list which roles can delegate them and who may receive them (example: Progress Report can be delegated by SO or AA on behalf of PI to PI or ASST; PI can delegate Progress Report to PI or ASST; SO can delegate Submit to PI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Delegation Authorities table for exact pairings and descriptions of what each authority enables (e.g., Progress Report allows working on Interim/Final RPPR and HSS requests; only SO can submit RPPRs unless they delegate Submit authority).

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation on behalf process constraints (search rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: When delegating authority on behalf of another user, you perform a two-step search: first locate the PI who currently holds the authority, then locate the PI/ASST to receive it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can enter an exact Commons ID (no wildcards allowed) or type a few letters of last name (name field must be last name, not first name) to get matches. Use the Select and then Edit Delegations flow and toggle the authority on, then Save.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegate progress report capability limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: When Progress Report authority is delegated to a PI/ASST, the delegate is able to initiate and work on progress reports for the delegator PI but the delegate is not able to route/submit (unless Submit authority is granted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The delegator PI can view delegates in My Current Delegates; the delegate receives email notification of change.
